newsitem.title: USA: US Plains cattle trade slow late in week -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains cattle trade slow late in week -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets remained quiet late Friday, with feedlot managers pricing next week's cattle $1.00 to $2.00 per cwt higher at $65.00 to $66.00 per cwt, feedlot sources said.
Some sources said meat packers may use Friday's bearishly-construed USDA Cattle-on-Feed report to bid lower for cattle Monday, possibly $63.00 per cwt.

The USDA report showed January placements at 125 percent of a year ago, which greatly exceeded trade estimates. CME live cattle futures were called to open 0.50 cent per lb lower in April on Tuesday and 1.00 cent lower in June and August.
Next week's showlists may be unchanged to slightly smaller than this week's, sources said.
A survey of major U.S. beef packers indicate most will be operating Monday, the U.S. President's Day holiday.
